parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station T-13 (survey area T). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1340.2 | 1.08 | 1.08
2 | 2148.3 | 1.38 | 2.46
3 | 5322.7 | 1.26 | 3.72
4 | 18475.7 | 0.33 | 4.05
5 | 19320.3 | - | -

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Station: T-13
Curve type: A-type (ρ1 < ρ2 < ρ3 < ρ4 < ρ5 – continuously ascending resistivity sequence)
Aquifer depth: 0 – 2.46 m (weathered/fractured zone overlying resistive bedrock)

Recommendation: The sharp rise in resistivity below 2.46 m (from ~5,300 to over 19,000 ohm‑m) indicates compact, unweathered, low-permeability bedrock with poor groundwater potential at this station. Drilling should target and case through the shallow weathered zone (0–2.46 m) for any yield, but given the thin saturated interval, the team should consider probing nearby VES points for a thicker weathered/fractured zone before committing to a full borehole here.
